clue.text: Read pitch badly, when going for a song

indicators.note: something done badly is botched or garbled, so the letters come out in a wrong order

blocks.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A singer misreads the pitch while performing a song.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical surface makes 'for a song' look like part of the performance; it is the idiom for very cheaply, and READ PITCH rearranges to DIRT CHEAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sold 'for a song' changes hands for a trifling price, the same idea as extremely inexpensive.

clue.text: Most attractive detective starts before end of August

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
a horse that starts in fright shies
the final letter of the month

explanation.surface: A handsome detective begins work just before the close of August.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts' reads as begins, but here it is the verb for jumping back in alarm, as a horse does. DI is the standard abbreviation for Detective Inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishy is informal British slang for good-looking, and its superlative names the person who is the best-looking.

clue.text: One getting up part of staircase

blocks.note: first meaning: a person who gets out of bed
second meaning: the vertical board between two treads

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone climbing a staircase, but the two halves are separate meanings of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a person leaving bed in the morning and the upright panel of each step.

clue.text: Electric looms weaving over time producing something desirable

indicators.note: weaving interlaces threads into new patterns, so the letters are worked into a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Power looms weaving away over a long period turn out something people want.
explanation.walkthrough: The looms are not machinery here: their letters, plus T for time, are rearranged into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A collector's item is an object prized and sought after by enthusiasts, so it is a thing people covet.

clue.text: Passion of English proposal

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting for debate

explanation.surface: An Englishman makes a passionate proposal, perhaps of marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proposal' suggests marriage, but it is the formal proposal debated at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Passion is strong feeling, and an emotion is any such feeling, so the two are close synonyms.

clue.text: Plant is different when covered in lead

indicators.note: something covered in a material is wrapped by it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
other means different

explanation.surface: A plant behaves strangely once it has been coated in lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' is the metal, given by its chemical symbol Pb from Latin plumbum, not a verb or a leash.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot herb is a plant grown for cooking, so it is one specific kind of plant.

clue.text: Correct flow returns

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the tide's flow is its rising movement

explanation.surface: The proper current comes back again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correct' looks like an adjective describing the flow, but it is the verb meaning to fix text.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to revise it and remove its errors, so it is a synonym of the verb correct.

clue.text: Rubbish record embarrassed Italian

blocks.note: a vinyl record is a disc
an embarrassed person goes red
IT is the abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: An Italian is mortified by a terrible record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' reads as an adjective describing the record, but it is the British verb meaning to criticise or dismiss.
explanation.definitionFit: To rubbish an idea, in informal British usage, is to disparage it and undermine its standing.

clue.text: Cast kicked around first bits of shoddy scenery

indicators.note: going around something means enclosing it, so one piece wraps another
the first bits of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: to toe a ball is to kick it with the tip of the foot
opening letters of both words

explanation.surface: Actors kick their way around a cheap, badly built stage set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the actors of a theatre company, which suits the scenery, but it is the past tense of the verb meaning to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast and tossed are both past forms of verbs for throwing something through the air.

clue.text: Complimentary trout garçon lays out, taking seconds

indicators.note: laying things out spreads them in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered
taking something means removing it, so a letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, without the cedilla
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for seconds; it is removed

explanation.surface: A French waiter sets out trout on the house, serving second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complimentary' suggests a free dish, but it means praising. 'Taking seconds' removes the S abbreviation for seconds from LAYS before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Complimentary remarks praise someone, just as congratulatory words express approval of their achievement.

clue.text: Plant in woods is a legume

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the following words, running across their joins

blocks.note: letters spanning the end of the first word through the start of the last

explanation.surface: A plant growing in the forest turns out to be a member of the pea family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legume' tempts as the definition, but the plant named at the start is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is an agave grown for its tough fibre, used for rope and matting, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Sheds unpopular families

blocks.note: out of favour, as in 'out' versus 'in'
a royal or noble family is a house, such as the House of Windsor

explanation.surface: Disliked families cast off something, as a snake sheds its skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheds' reads like a verb, but it is the plural noun for garden huts.
explanation.definitionFit: Outhouses are small outbuildings attached to a main house, just as garden huts are.

clue.text: Middle Eastern serial about head of intelligence

indicators.note: about can mean scattered around, so these letters are moved into a new order
the head of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A television drama from the Middle East about a spy chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' suggests subject matter, but it signals rearranging the letters of SERIAL together with I.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel lies in the Middle East, so the adjective for that country is a specific Middle Eastern nationality.

clue.text: Make a pig of oneself from beans regularly found next to valley

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter is taken

blocks.note: second and fourth letters
a gorge is a narrow, steep-sided valley

explanation.surface: Someone overeats from a regular supply of beans beside a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: The beans give only every other letter, starting from the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To engorge is to gorge or stuff yourself with food, which is what a greedy eater does.

clue.text: Piece of wood going around table

blocks.note: skirting something means passing around its edge
a board is a table, as in 'board and lodging'

explanation.surface: A length of timber is fitted around a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going around table' looks like a description of where the wood goes, but it splits into two synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirting board is the wooden strip fixed along the base of an interior wall, so it is a timber length.

clue.text: One male graduate with weapon shows lack of equilibrium

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the abbreviation for male
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree holder
a lance is a long spear

explanation.surface: A young male graduate wielding a weapon is unsteady on his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: Four short pieces join in order; BA is the usual crossword graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbalance is a state where forces or quantities are unequal, so balance or stability is missing.

clue.text: Border of France about level

blocks.note: FR is the abbreviation for France
on means about, as in a book on birds
a tier is one level of a structure

explanation.surface: France's border runs roughly flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a container or reversal signal, but here it is simply ON, meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontier is the dividing line between two countries, exactly what a national border is.

clue.text: One after a good deal of profit in treatment of heartburn

indicators.note: something in another is held inside it, so one piece goes within the other
treating material processes and reworks it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: Someone who stands to profit a lot from a remedy for indigestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A good deal of profit' sounds like a large amount, but 'a good deal' belongs to the definition, a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain hunter shops around looking for cheap purchases, so they are always chasing a bargain.

clue.text: Increase dispersal of mutagen

indicators.note: dispersal scatters things in all directions, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Spreading a mutation-causing agent makes things worse.
explanation.walkthrough: The scientific term is only fodder: its seven letters rearrange exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: To augment something is to make it larger or add to it, a direct synonym of the verb increase.

clue.text: Bit of pen point leaked

blocks.note: the nib is the writing tip of a pen
ink bleeds when it leaks through paper

explanation.surface: A small piece of the pen's tip let out ink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit' reads as a small piece, but it is the past tense of bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Nibbling is taking small bites, so the past tense of nibble matches a past tense of the verb bite.

clue.text: Scrap rotten bit of meat

blocks.note: food that has gone off is rotten
a cut is a piece of meat from a butcher

explanation.surface: Throw away that piece of meat which has gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' reads as a verb telling you to discard the meat, but it is the noun for a leftover piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An offcut is a leftover piece trimmed from wood, cloth or paper, the same as a remnant or scrap.

clue.text: Substantial contents

blocks.note: first meaning: of a meal, satisfying the appetite
second meaning: what goes inside a pie, sandwich or tooth cavity

explanation.walkthrough: Two words that look like a description of a book's contents are separate senses of one word: an adjective and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearty meal is described as satisfying in this way, and the stuffing inside a pie or sandwich has the same name.

clue.text: Fern's underwear caught by Barbie's partner

blocks.note: a bra is an item of women's underwear
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
Ken is the boyfriend doll of Barbie

explanation.surface: A woman named Fern has her underwear grabbed by Ken, Barbie's boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fern' looks like a woman's name, but it is the definition. 'Caught by' reads like a container but is C followed by the next piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracken is a large, coarse fern that covers heaths and hillsides across Britain.

clue.text: Jack drove van kilometres partly in reverse

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them
going in reverse means travelling backwards, so the letters read right to left

blocks.note: a run of letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: A man called Jack drove a van some distance backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like the driver's name, but it is the playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: In a pack of cards the jack is also called the knave, the court card ranking below the queen.

clue.text: Conservative German, taking drug repeatedly, left fish

blocks.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative
Ger is the abbreviation for German
E is slang for the drug ecstasy, here given twice
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A conservative German keeps taking drugs and then abandons a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb meaning abandoned, but it is the direction abbreviation. E for ecstasy is a standard crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A conger eel is a large sea-dwelling eel, and eels are a kind of fish.

clue.text: Beast rejected beer following fine

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters go back the way they came
following means coming after, so the piece before this word is placed second

blocks.note: OK means fine or all right
IPA is India Pale Ale, a type of beer

explanation.surface: An animal turns down a pint after paying a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' suggests a penalty, but it means all right; 'following' puts the beer after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a forest-dwelling African mammal related to the giraffe, so it is a wild animal.

clue.text: Squad heard to swarm

indicators.note: what is heard is what reaches the ear, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: a squad is a sports team

explanation.surface: A team is reported to crowd together.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the verb at the end; the sports group only supplies the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To teem is to be crowded or overflowing with living things, as a swarm is.

clue.text: Toy torpedo boat initially circling whirlpool getting attention

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word gives only its first letter
circling something means going all the way round it, so those letters enclose another piece

blocks.note: first letters of both words
an eddy is a small whirlpool
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A toy torpedo boat goes round a whirlpool and draws a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toy' looks like an adjective describing the boat, but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A teddy bear is a soft stuffed animal for children, one of the most familiar toys.
